frameworks.name: 60-Second Diagnostic for Scaling Healthcare Services
frameworks.definition: A rapid diagnosis framework that identifies the binding constraint in a service business by asking: who is the ideal customer, what existing asset can reach them, and where is the gap in the sales execution.

frameworks.name: Trusted Asset Leverage for Lead Generation
frameworks.definition: Using an existing credibility asset (podcast appearance, media exposure) as the primary lead magnet, combined with geographic targeting and active sales follow-up to convert awareness into customers.

claims.text: In service businesses with high close rates (70%+), the binding constraint is typically top-of-funnel lead volume, not sales mechanics—the business can absorb more customers but lacks an efficient customer acquisition system (Alex Hormozi, healthcare context).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: A high close rate signals strong product-market fit and sales conversion; the business is not constrained by closing ability but by the number of qualified leads entering the pipeline.
bounded_by: Does not apply to low-close-rate businesses where sales mechanics need fixing
Does not apply when supply/fulfillment capacity is the true constraint

claims.text: For a service business with an existing credibility asset (e.g., podcast guest appearance), the first move is to identify the geographic center of your ideal customer within 50 miles of your location and drive traffic from that defined audience to the credibility asset, then measure downstream conversion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Geographic proximity combined with knowing the authority figure (Rogan-featured doctor) creates high purchase intent; a 50-mile radius filters for customers for whom travel is feasible and proximity to the expert creates decision weight.

anchors.value: Dramatically higher probability of follow-up than national broadcast audience

bounded_by: Assumes practice has geographic flexibility; inapplicable to purely telehealth models
Requires existing earned media credibility to work

claims.text: Most healthcare practices have zero dedicated sales staff, making them unable to execute proactive lead follow-up (e.g., checking if prospects watched the podcast, identifying pain points, converting awareness into appointments)—this gap is the primary sales execution bottleneck.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Without dedicated sales staff, inbound interest converts to active appointments only if the prospect self-initiates; proactive follow-up—which bridges the awareness-to-action gap—is completely absent.
bounded_by: Applies primarily to high-touch service delivery models
Does not apply to fully self-serve or fully provider-initiated booking models

claims.text: A published or earned-media podcast or video asset functions as a video sales letter when distributed to a defined audience; it prequalifies prospects by self-selection (people watch because the topic interests them) and carries the authority of the original publication (e.g., Joe Rogan's platform).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Asset is standalone complete episode or segment
Audience has known interest in the topic
claims.mechanism: The original publication's credibility (Rogan's platform) transfers to the featured expert; viewers self-select by choosing to watch (implicit interest signal); the expert's demonstration of capability within the content reduces perceived risk in the buyer's mind.
bounded_by: Does not work with fragmented or clickbait clips
Requires the original publication to have relevant authority for your audience

claims.text: Driving traffic from a qualified audience directly to an existing earned-media asset (rather than creating new marketing materials) avoids regulatory risk in healthcare because the physician is not making claims—only directing people to a pre-existing editorial piece.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Directing traffic to an editorial piece is promotion of the media outlet, not promotion of medical services; this distinction preserves compliance while still creating lead flow.
bounded_by: Does not remove the need to comply with follow-up communication regulations
Assumes the editorial piece itself made no prohibited claims

claims.text: A service business with national demand can significantly increase close rate and customer value by focusing acquisition efforts on a concentrated geographic region, because local proximity to the expert creates decision urgency and feasibility for customers.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Expert has built credibility (e.g., media visibility)
claims.mechanism: Knowing the expert is geographically proximate and created the result the customer heard about creates urgency and decision confidence; travel is feasible; competition from other local experts is reduced.

anchors.value: Small fraction interested + high friction (travel unknown)
Higher fraction interested + feasible travel + urgency

bounded_by: Does not apply if fulfillment capacity is already exceeded within the local region

examples.text: An orthopedic surgeon specializing in regenerative medicine grew from an insurance-based practice to $2.1M in annual revenue by pivoting to cash-based services, then earned credibility through a Joe Rogan podcast appearance featuring their treatment approach. The challenge was that awareness (from Rogan) did not automatically convert to lead volume, despite high close rates (80%+) on prospects who did reach the practice. Alex Hormozi recommended identifying the 50-mile local radius of patients for whom the Rogan-featured doctor's location was feasible and driving targeted audience to the podcast episode, then adding a dedicated sales person to follow up with viewers who watched and probe for pain points, converting interested viewers into appointment bookings.

A healthcare practice promoting a Joe Rogan podcast appearance can use paid ads to drive traffic to the YouTube episode rather than creating new advertising materials. This approach avoids FDA/FTC compliance risk because the practice is promoting an editorial piece (Rogan's show), not making direct service claims, while still leveraging the publication's credibility and the expert's visibility.

practices.text: Once traffic is driven to the podcast episode or video asset, assign a dedicated sales staff member to proactively follow up with viewers using low-pressure inquiry: 'Did you get a chance to watch the podcast? What was most interesting to you?' This bridges the gap from awareness to scheduled appointment.

For healthcare practices with geographic flexibility, prioritize customer acquisition within a defined radius (e.g., 50 miles) rather than pursuing national leads, as local proximity dramatically increases both decision likelihood and revenue quality.

Use a multi-method diagnostic when scaling: after identifying that top-of-funnel is the constraint, explore whether the best customer acquisition path is affiliate partnerships, content distribution, or paid advertising—choose based on organizational capability and risk tolerance.
